The series is set on the small fictional Caribbean island of Saint Marie. The premise is that a British Detective Inspector is dispatched reluctantly to the island to solve the murder of a policeman and remains to solve further crimes against his will, in conjunction with the local police. In subsequent seasons further British detectives replace the original, usually with a similar degree of reluctance. The plots combine gentle murder mystery with primarily culture clash comedy. The show is broadcast on [[BBC One]] in the United Kingdom, [[France 2]] in France, [[PBS]] in the United States, [[Prime (New Zealand TV channel)|Prime]] in New Zealand (with repeats on [[BBC UKTV]]) and [[Foxtel]]'s BBC First channel, [[ABC (Australian TV channel)|ABC]], [[9Gem]] in Australia, with repeat episodes on [[Atreseries]] in Spain. The series was inspired by a real-life event when [[Bob Woolmer]], the coach of the [[Pakistan national cricket team]], died in suspicious circumstances in [[Jamaica]] during the [[2007 Cricket World Cup]] and British policeman [[Mark Shields (police officer)|Mark Shields]] of the [[Jamaica Constabulary Force]] led the murder investigation.{{Cite web |title=Robert Thorogood, Creator of Death In Paradise |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/mediapacks/death-in-paradise/robert-thorogood |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=www.bbc.co.uk |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Townsend |first1=Mark |title=Bob Woolmer: The murder that never was |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2007/jul/01/cricket.features |access-date=19 July 2026 |work=[[The Observer]] |date=30 June 2007}} Since its 2011 debut, ''Death in Paradise'' has enjoyed high viewing figures and a generally positive critical reception, leading to repeated renewals.{{cite web |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2013-02-12/death-in-paradise-series-three-confirmed |title=Death in Paradise series three confirmed |website=Radio Times |date=12 February 2013}} The show is |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-future-confirmed-newsupdate/ |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Radio Times |language=en-GB}} A [[Spinoff (media)|spin-off]] series, ''[[Beyond Paradise (TV series)|Beyond Paradise]]'', began airing in 2023 with Marshall reprising his role of DI Humphrey Goodman, while a second spin-off, ''[[Return to Paradise (2024 TV series)|Return to Paradise]]'', began airing in 2024.{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/2023/return-to-paradise | title=BBC One and iPlayer will Return to Paradise |website=BBC}} ==Synopsis== {{Anchor|Plot}} Detective Inspector [[Richard Poole (character)|Richard Poole]] ([[Ben Miller]]) is sent from the [[Metropolitan Police]] in London to investigate the murder of Charlie Hulme, a British police officer on the fictional Caribbean island of Saint Marie, a [[British Overseas Territory]] with a French colonial history.{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01pvmf6 |title=BBC One – Death in Paradise |website=BBC |date=26 February 2015 |access-date=30 March 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-filming-location/ |title=Where is Death in Paradise filmed? |website=radiotimes.com |date=23 December 2021 |access-date=8 March 2023}} After he finds the murderer (later revealed to be Sergeant Lily Thompson), he is ordered by his supervisors to stay on as the [[Divisional detective inspector|Detective Inspector]] (DI) of the island, much to his dismay, solving new cases as they appear and being the object of many fish-out-of-water jokes.{{cite web |url=http://alibi.uktv.co.uk/death-in-paradise/article/about-death-in-paradise-series-1/ |title=About Series 1 | Death in Paradise | Alibi Channel |publisher=Alibi.uktv.co.uk |access-date=30 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108173144/http://alibi.uktv.co.uk/death-in-paradise/article/about-death-in-paradise-series-1/ |archive-date=8 January 2015 |url-status=dead}} At the start of series 3, Poole is himself murdered while attending a 25th anniversary party and clumsy London DI [[Humphrey Goodman]] ([[Kris Marshall]]) arrives to investigate the death of his [[deadpan]] predecessor. After he finds the murderer (later revealed to be Helen Reed), he stays on the island permanently after learning from his wife, Sally, that she is leaving him. In the second half of series 6, he resigns so he can start a new life in London with his new girlfriend Martha Lloyd (who he later marries), after forming a relationship with her while she was staying at Saint Marie on holiday. Goodman's replacement on Saint Marie is DI [[Jack Mooney]] ([[Ardal O'Hanlon]]), a recent widower grieving the loss of his wife and who assisted the team on a case in London. Mooney embraces island life and remains on Saint Marie until mid-way through series 9, when he decides he is ready to face the memory of his deceased wife and returns to London to be with his daughter. Mooney's replacement is DI Neville Parker ([[Ralf Little]]), who, like DI Poole before him, initially dislikes being on the island and has severe allergies, especially to bug bites. He comes to the island only because the team needs a British detective to sign off on a case and is forced to stay longer after a period of illness renders him temporarily unfit to travel. However, he decides to remain on the island and eventually warms to the island lifestyle. He stays until series 13, when he departs to travel and be in a relationship with former [[Sergeant#Police|Detective Sergeant]] (DS) [[Florence Cassell]] ([[Joséphine Jobert]]), who joined the team initially as an Officer after Sergeant Fidel Best departed following series 3. During the [[Christmas]] 2024 special, Commissioner Selwyn Patterson ([[Don Warrington]]) calls London for yet another replacement DI to lead investigations in Saint Marie. Mervin Wilson ([[Don Gilet]]) happens to be visiting the island on holiday. As he is boarding the aircraft to take him away from the 'slow-paced' island, he receives a telephone call from his superior ordering him to stay and solve the murder. Although Wilson is annoyed by island life (much like DIs Poole and, initially, Parker before him), a personal connection to Saint Marie spurs him to remain there. ==Episodes== {{Main|List of Death in Paradise episodes}} {{:List of Death in Paradise episodes}} ==Format== The show is known for its [[formulaic]] approach to its plots{{cite web|last=Watson |first=Keith |url=http://metro.co.uk/2014/03/04/death-in-paradise-did-have-its-quirks-but-it-was-too-formulaic-and-a-touch-lazy-4411706/|title=Death In Paradise did have its quirks but it was too formulaic and a touch lazy |website=Metro|date=4 March 2014|access-date=14 December 2016}} with each episode roughly the same in length, style and narrative structure. Each episode begins with a pre-credits sequence showing the events leading up to a murder and often the discovery of the body afterwards; this sequence also serves to introduce that particular episode's guest characters.{{cite web|url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2016-01-07/the-secrets-of-death-in-paradise|title=The secrets of Death in Paradise 7 January 2016|website=Radio Times|access-date=14 December 2016}} The police force of Saint Marie is subsequently informed of the murder, preliminary investigations and interviews take place to establish the suspects, and photographs of the suspects and crime scene are placed on the [[whiteboard]] at police headquarters.{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Death-in-Paradise-Season-4/dp/B00SFXV4DQ|title=Success in Paradise!!!! 28 February 2015|website=Amazon|access-date=14 December 2016}} The crime often presents an apparently impossible feature, with a [[closed circle of suspects]], all of whom have motive but none of whom appear to have had opportunity. They either present what seem to be airtight alibis for the time the crime was believed to have committed, or the crime is a [[locked-room mystery]], with the victim being found in circumstances that appear to make it impossible that anyone could have entered or left the location without being observed. Often towards the end, the lead DI will have a moment of realisation, perhaps brought on by something that someone says or does, or by some occurrence. At this moment, the [[Means, motive, and opportunity|how, why, and who]] of the murder are comprehended by the DI, but are not revealed to the audience. The suspects are then gathered, and the DI talks through the evidence; often, [[flashback (narrative)|flashbacks]] are used to show what happened. The murderer and the motive are revealed in the [[Detective dénouement|dénouement]] of the episode.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/tvandradioblog/2013/feb/11/death-in-paradise-how-viewers|title=Death in Paradise: how on earth does this get so many viewers? 12 February 2013|website=[[The Guardian]] |date=11 February 2013|access-date=14 December 2016}} Gathering the suspects, going through the events and finally identifying and arresting the murderer is based on the technique [[Agatha Christie]] uses in the ''[[Miss Marple]]'' stories and some of the ''[[Hercule Poirot]]'' ones. Normally, each episode ends with a comedic scene or a celebratory trip by the police officers to Catherine's bar.{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R1OWDDZRQKSFZ3/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_viewpnt?ASIN=B00D49YE4W |title=Harmless Nonsense, Nice Palm Trees |website=Amazon|access-date=14 December 2016}} The final episode of most series has included a subplot wherein the lead DI is tempted to return to the UK by the prospect of a job offer or personal relationship, but in the end, he decides to remain on the island. This format was subverted in the sixth series, when the two-part storyline in the fifth and sixth episodes saw the team travel to London to follow up on a current case, resulting in Goodman deciding to remain to be with his new girlfriend, Martha; Mooney travelled back to Saint-Marie, initially as a holiday to help escape the memory of his recently deceased wife, but decided to remain as the new detective inspector of the island. This format was also subverted in the ninth series; Mooney decided to return to Britain mid-way through the series as he felt that he was ready to face the memory of his dead wife, with the new inspector (DI Neville Parker) initially coming to the island just to sign off on a particular body but kept for a few weeks for health reasons before he decided to remain to face a new challenge. Parker remains the DI on the island until the end of Series 13, when he departs the island to go travelling with his former DS Florence Cassell. His replacement, DI Mervin Wilson, initially just ended up working with the team by chance in the 2024 Christmas special as he was on holiday on the island when a difficult case came up, but he was subsequently convinced to sign a three-month contract to remain on the island that he later chose to extend. While ''Death in Paradise'' has continued to be in the top three most popular programmes on British television, critics have called the crime drama "unremarkable" and "an undemanding detective show, with nice Caribbean scenery."{{cite news | first=Jack | last=Seale | title=What is the Secret to Death in Paradise? |work=[[The Guardian]] | date=19 February 2015 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/tvandradioblog/2015/feb/19/the-secret-to-death-in-paradises-success-is-simplicity-and-sunshine}} ==Setting== ===Saint Marie=== [[File:Deshaies.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Deshaies]] on [[Guadeloupe]], which is used for the town of Honoré in ''Death in Paradise''.]] ''Death in Paradise'' is set on the fictional Caribbean island of Saint Marie, described in episode 3.3 as a "pretty island" that is "situated in the Eastern [[Caribbean Sea]]". In episode 4.5, it is mentioned that Martinique is "a good 70 miles". Saint Marie is "one-tenth the size of its north-west neighbour [[Guadeloupe]]"; this would make Saint Marie about {{convert|63|sqmi}} in size. Saint Marie is a [[British Overseas Territory]], but about 30% of its people are French, due to its previous history, with the [[French language|language]] still widely spoken. The back-story appears to be a blend of two real-world islands near Guadeloupe, with size and location aligning with [[Marie-Galante]] and history and language aligning with [[Dominica]]. In the TV show, the fictional Saint Marie island has a [[volcano]], [[rainforest]], [[sugar plantation]]s, a fishing harbour, an airport, a university, a convent, approximately 100 public beaches and a [[Crown Court]]. It also has its own newspaper, ''The Saint Marie Times'', a radio station, ''Radio Saint Marie'', and a television station, ''Saint Marie Broadcasting Corporation'' (SMBC). Its vehicles have French number plates, and motor vehicles drive on the right. Police uniforms are also French, not British. The police hierarchy is a blend of French and British, as the Detective Inspectors are British and the Commissioner reports to the Chief Commissioner in Jamaica (formerly a British territory), while the Internal Affairs team is from France. Honoré, the name of the main town, is a reference to St Honoré, the setting of ''[[A Caribbean Mystery]]'' by [[Agatha Christie]]. The town has a leisure/commercial [[marina]], market, bars and restaurants as well as the police station. The neighbouring town to Honoré is named Port Royal. Saint Marie's main economic ties are to Guadeloupe, the UK and France. The island's main religions are [[Catholicism]] and [[African diaspora religions|Voodoo]], with several religious festivals featuring in the programme, including the [[Saint Ursula]] Festival (in reality, a major festival of the [[Virgin Islands]]) and some Voodoo festivals.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}} ===Other locations=== Series 3, episode 7 is largely set on an islet just off Saint Marie; it is privately owned and relatively small. This episode was actually filmed on the island of Kahouanne, around {{convert|1.2|mi}} off the northwest coast of [[Guadeloupe]] where the series is normally filmed. It can often be seen in the background from a beach on Saint Marie. Series 6, Episodes 5 and 6 are largely set in London, when Goodman, Cassell, and Officer Myers form a liaison team with Mooney in order to track down suspects in a murder investigation in Saint Marie and later to investigate the murder of one of the suspects. Season 15 episode 6 takes place mainly on the (real) island of [[Antigua]] Other fictional islands (Saint Felix, Saint Helene, Saint Barnabas, and Saint Auguste) have featured throughout the series, with the Saint Marie police responsible for overseeing their local law enforcement. ==Characters== {{See also|List of Death in Paradise characters}} ===Main=== * [[Ben Miller]] as Detective Inspector (DI) [[Richard Poole (character)|Richard Poole]] (series 1-2; guest series 3, 10) * [[Sara Martins]] as Detective Sergeant (DS) [[Camille Bordey]] (series 1-4; guest series 10, 13) * [[Danny John-Jules]] as Officer Dwayne Myers (series 1-7, 13, 2024 Special; guest 2021 Special) * [[Gary Carr (actor)|Gary Carr]] as Officer/Sergeant Fidel Best (series 1-3) * [[Don Warrington]] as Commissioner Selwyn Patterson (series 1-present) * [[Élizabeth Bourgine]] as Catherine Bordey (later mayor of Honoré, the main town of Saint Marie), Camille's mother and owner of Catherine's Bar (series 2-present; recurring series 1) * [[Kris Marshall]] as Detective Inspector (DI) [[Humphrey Goodman]] (series 3-6) * [[Joséphine Jobert]] as Officer/Sergeant/Detective Sergeant (DS) [[Florence Cassell]] (series 4-8, 10-11; recurring series 13) * [[Tobi Bakare]] as Officer/Sergeant Jean-Pierre "J.P." [[Danny John-Jules]], the longest-tenured actor in the series not named [[Don Warrington]] or [[Elizabeth Bourgine]], did not return for series eight and was replaced by Shyko Amos.{{cite web|url=https://www.smoothradio.com/news/entertainment/death-in-paradise-series-8-cast/|title=Death in Paradise axes longtime star Danny John Jules as Dwayne|website=Smooth}} John-Jules cited his reason for exiting the show as wanting to leave "on a high."{{cite web|url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/tv/2018-04-26/how-when-and-why-is-danny-john-jules-leaving-death-in-paradise/|title=How, when and why is Danny John-Jules leaving Death in Paradise?|website=Radio Times|access-date=21 June 2018|archive-date=30 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180530201046/http://www.radiotimes.com/news/tv/2018-04-26/how-when-and-why-is-danny-john-jules-leaving-death-in-paradise/|url-status=dead}} Both Amos and Aude Legastelois-Bidé left at the conclusion of series 9. John-Jules would later return for series 13. === Harry === In addition to the human characters, a recurring animal character is "Harry," a lizard who lives at the Detective Inspector's shack. He appears in almost every episode and acts as a sounding board for the Detective Inspector to discuss the status of the current case and his life experiences. Harry is computer-generated.{{Cite web |author=David Hollingsworth |date=2023-07-17 |title=Death in Paradise reveals Harry the Lizard secret |url=https://www.whattowatch.com/news/death-in-paradise-reveals-harry-the-lizard-secret |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=What to Watch |language=en}} ==Production== [[File:Death in Paradise cast photo.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The original team (left-to-right): Sara Martins, Danny John-Jules, Gary Carr and Ben Miller]] [[File:Église de Deshaies - rue de l'Église.JPG|thumb|right|Deshaies' church is right next to the fictional "Honoré police station".]] [[File:View of the Presbytery at Deshaies (Guadeloupe, ca. 1850s), which serves as the police station in the TV series "Death in Paradise.".jpg|thumb|View of the Presbytery at Deshaies (Guadeloupe, c.1850s), which serves as the police station]] The series is filmed on the French archipelago of [[Guadeloupe]] in the [[Lesser Antilles]], mainly in the commune of [[Deshaies]] (which doubles for the town of Honoré on the fictional island of Saint Marie), with the help of the ''Bureau d'accueil des tournages de la Région Guadeloupe.''{{cite web|url=http://www.guadeloupe.franceantilles.fr/loisirs/une-tv-mag/meurtre-au-paradis-l-industrie-du-cinema-teste-la-guadeloupe-16-09-2011-138871.php |title=Meurtre au paradis. L'industrie du cinéma teste la Guadeloupe – Abonnement |website=Guadeloupe.franceantilles.fr |date=16 September 2011 |access-date=30 March 2015}} The site of the Honoré police station is a church hall in Deshaies (built c.1850s),{{cite web|url=http://colonialarchitectureproject.org/index?/category/4004-deshaies_presbytery|title=French Empire / Guadeloupe / Religious / Deshaies, Presbytery |work=Colonial Architecture Project}} with the priest's office appearing as the incident room.{{cite web|last=Skinitis |first=Alexia |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2017-01-05/death-in-paradise-head-to-guadeloupe-for-a-sundowner-at-humphrey-goodmans-favourite-beach |title=Where is Death in Paradise filmed? Guadeloupe location guide |work=Radio Times |date=5 January 2017 |access-date=24 February 2017}} Filming series 1 was particularly difficult, due to the lack of infrastructure in [[Guadeloupe]] for long-term filming, as well as the fact that [[Sara Martins]], the actress who plays [[Camille Bordey|DS Camille Bordey]], broke her leg in the middle of filming, causing her to be almost entirely written out of episode 6 of series 1 and causing difficulties during the filming of episodes 7 and 8.{{cite web|title=10 years of Death in Paradise: The story of everyone's favourite Caribbean crime drama – and its enduring success|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-story-10-years-rt-rewind-exclusive/|access-date=12 February 2021|website=Radio Times|language=en}} Miller left the series at the start of series 3, as he felt he was spending too much time away from his family, since his wife was unable to join him on the island during production. Marshall's family joined him on the island during his first three six-month shoots and his son, Thomas, enrolled at a local school. When his family could not join him during the filming of the sixth series, following the birth of his baby daughter, Elsie, it left him feeling "bereft and empty" and he subsequently decided to leave the show.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-38839073 |title=Kris Marshall swaps Death In Paradise for family time |work=BBC News |date=2 February 2017 |access-date=24 February 2017}} From episode 7 of the sixth series, the lead role was taken by [[Ardal O'Hanlon]] playing DI Jack Mooney, a London colleague.{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b08fp6w8 |title=BBC One - Death in Paradise, Series 6, Episode 7 |work=BBC |date=16 February 2017 |access-date=24 February 2017}} [[Joséphine Jobert]] left the series after episode 6 of the eighth series and was replaced by actress Aude Legastelois, who plays Madeleine Dumas. Jobert cited her reason for exiting the show as wanting to "focus on other projects". O'Hanlon confirmed he had left the show in October 2019, with his last appearance coming in series 9, episode 4.{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/latestnews/2019/ardal-ohanlon-death-in-paradise |title= Ardal O'Hanlon waves goodbye to BBC One drama Death In Paradise |website=BBC Media Centre}} His replacement, [[Ralf Little]] who plays DI Neville Parker, was revealed the same month.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/latestnews/2019/ralf-little-joins-death-in-paradise|title = Ralf Little to join cast of BBC One drama Death in Paradise |website=BBC Media Centre}} In July 2020, the BBC announced the departure of Shyko Amos and Legastelois, along with the return of Jobert and the arrival of newcomer [[Tahj Miles]] as Marlon Pryce.{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a33410831/death-in-paradise-season-10-florence-josephine-jobert-return/ |title=Death in Paradise bringing back major character as filming resumes |work=Digital Spy |date=24 July 2020 |access-date=25 July 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-cast-season-10/ |title=Meet the cast of Death in Paradise season 10 |work=[[Radio Times]] |date=11 February 2021 |access-date=23 February 2024}} In January 2022, in the fourth episode of series 11, Jobert left the show for the second time after her character left the island. Her departure had not been previously announced. She returned again for the third time in series 13, episode six, broadcast in March 2024. Meanwhile, [[Tahj Miles]] departed the island as Marlon Pryce the episode beforehand, he was replaced by Dwayne Myers, who had previously left. [[Ralf Little]] departs as Neville at the end of the series, with Florence, as they express their love for each other.{{cite web|last=Iftikhar |first=Asyia |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a38927791/death-in-paradise-character-exit-fans-heartbroken/ |title=Death in Paradise fans left heartbroken over character exit |website=Digital Spy |date=28 January 2022 |access-date=13 March 2022}} ==Reception== ===Viewing figures=== ''Death in Paradise'' has gained popularity over time on British TV. Series 1 (2011) has been the least-watched to date, averaging 5.89 million viewers, with the 5.3 million viewers for the sixth episode, "An Unhelpful Aid", being the lowest the show has had. Each episode was among the top five most-watched programmes of the day and in the top 40 of the week.{{cite web |date=13 January 2021 |title=Murder mystery: how Death in Paradise quietly became one of TV's biggest hits |url=http://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2021/jan/13/mystery-how-death-in-paradise-quietly-became-one-of-tvs-biggest-hits |access-date=7 June 2022 |website=[[The Guardian]] |language=en}}{{Failed verification|date=June 2022}} Series 2 (2013) averaged 7.67 million viewers, with each episode among the top two most-watched programmes of the day and in the top 15 of the week.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} Series 3 (2014) averaged 8.46 million viewers, with each episode among the top two most-watched programmes of the day and in the top ten of the week.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} Series 4 (2015) averaged 9.03 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode was among the top three most-watched programmes of the day and in the top ten of the week.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} Series 5 (2016) averaged 8.67 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode was the most-watched programme of the day and in the top four of the week.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} Series 6 (2017) has been the most-watched so far, averaging 9.1 million viewers. The series premiere, "Erupting in Murder", is the most-watched episode of the show to date with 9.81 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode of Series 6 was the most-watched programme of the day and in the top four of the week.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} Series 7 (2018) averaged 8.34 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode was the most-watched programme of the day and in the top ten of the week.{{cite web|url=http://www.barb.co.uk/viewing-data/weekly-top-30/?_s=4|title=Weekly top 30 programmes |work=BARB }} Series 8 (2019) averaged 8.2 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode was the most-watched programme of the day and in the top seven of the week. Series 9 (2020) averaged 8.14 million viewers. Based on consolidated figures, each episode was the most-watched programme of the day and in the top six of the week.{{cite web|url=https://www.barb.co.uk/viewing-data/four-screen-dashboard/|title=Weekly top programmes on four screens (from Sept 2018) |work=BARB }} According to a ''Radio Times'' article in 2018, "From Australia to Russia to India, stretching across 236 territories, this British crime comedy-drama has become a global phenomenon."{{cite web|title=How Death in Paradise conquered the world|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/how-death-in-paradise-conquered-the-world/|access-date=26 April 2021|website=Radio Times|language=en-US}} ===Critical response=== The series has received mixed reviews from critics, with most criticism directed towards its formulaic structure. The first series was praised for its refreshing style and setting. Kris Marshall's introduction at the start of series 3 was particularly well received, with Rebecca Smith of ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' citing Marshall as a "winning addition" to the cast.{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/10568337/Death-in-Paradise-episode-one-review.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/10568337/Death-in-Paradise-episode-one-review.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Death in Paradise, episode one, review |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |date=14 January 2014 |first=Rebecca |last=Smith |access-date=30 March 2015}}{{cbignore}} The series 4 premiere was described as "a little piece of escapism" and was generally praised. Mark Monahan of ''The Daily Telegraph'' criticised the laid-back tone of the series, calling it too methodical with nothing unique about it besides the setting.{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/11349482/Death-in-Paradise-series-4-episode-2-review-too-tame.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/11349482/Death-in-Paradise-series-4-episode-2-review-too-tame.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Death in Paradise, review: 'too tame' |publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |date=15 January 2015 |first=Mark |last=Monahan |access-date=30 March 2015}}{{cbignore}} There have also been media comments about [[colonialism]] and [[racism]].{{cite web |last=Watson |first=Keith |date=25 October 2011 |title=Death In Paradise was an easy watch but left a slightly sour taste |url=https://metro.co.uk/2011/10/25/death-in-paradise-series-1-episode-1-tv-review-194925/ |access-date=15 July 2022 |website=Metro |language=en}} After the first episode aired in 2011, ''[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]'' TV critic Keith Watson wrote that "the idea of parachuting a policeman into a colonial setting because the locals weren't up to the job left a slightly sour taste," and the series resembled a "throwback to the fading glory days of the [[British Empire]]". In a January 2021 ''[[The Guardian|Guardian]]'' essay, writer Sirin Kale pointed out the "large and appreciative audience", but was critical of several aspects, including the racial dynamics: "If Death in Paradise was a dated show when it aired – a throwback to [[Peter Falk]] in a trench coat asking [[Columbo (character)|just one more thing]] – it is a museum piece now. For starters, the cast of mostly Black supporting actors call the show's white, male lead 'Sir', and rely on him to solve crimes that are apparently beyond their wits to work out."{{cite web|date=13 January 2021|title=Murder mystery: how Death in Paradise quietly became one of TV's biggest hits|url=http://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2021/jan/13/mystery-how-death-in-paradise-quietly-became-one-of-tvs-biggest-hits|access-date=7 April 2021|website=[[The Guardian]] |language=en}} ===Awards=== {{Anchor|Awards|Accolades}} Red Planet Pictures was nominated for, and won, the "Diversity in a Drama Production Award" for ''Death in Paradise''. Sara Martins, Danny John-Jules, Don Warrington and Tobi Bakare collected the award at a ceremony supported by the BBC and ITV that took place on 15 February 2015.{{cite web|work=Red Planet Pictures|title=Death in Paradise Wins Award|url=http://www.redplanetpictures.co.uk/news/16/19/Death-In-Paradise-Wins-Award|date=20 February 2015|access-date=27 February 2015|archive-date=27 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227200759/http://www.redplanetpictures.co.uk/news/16/19/Death-In-Paradise-Wins-Award|url-status=dead}} ==Broadcast== In the UK, all series are shown on [[BBC One]]. The first series was broadcast in late 2011. The second series was broadcast in January 2013, with subsequent series filling the same January slot; all series were shown in a 9:00–10:00 pm slot.{{efn|Series 4, episode 7 was shown earlier at 8.25 pm-9.25 pm due to ''[[EastEnders]]'' Live 30th anniversary celebrations.}} In France the programme is broadcast on [[France 2]] and [[France Ô]]. ''Death in Paradise'' is broadcast in 236 territories.{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/news/tv/2018-02-26/how-death-in-paradise-conquered-the-world/|title=How Death in Paradise conquered the world|website=Radio Times|access-date=5 March 2019}} The entire series has been available to stream all year around since May 2020 on [[Britbox]].{{cite web|url=https://www.britbox.com/us/show/Death_in_Paradise_24258|title=Death in Paradise S1 - Mystery | BritBox|access-date=14 May 2020|archive-date=1 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401230500/https://www.britbox.com/us/show/Death_in_Paradise_24258|url-status=dead}} In the USA the programme appears on a number of [[PBS]] stations. The show is currently{{when?|date=July 2025}} featured on [[Ovation (American TV channel)|Ovation]]'s "Morning Mysteries" block on Fridays, and also used to air on the network every Thursday night at 7PM with back-to-back episodes. Also in the USA, as of 1 April 2026, Pluto TV streams DIP episodes in a marathon manner on Fridays and Saturdays. [https://www.amazon.com/Death-Paradise-Season-Fifteen-DVD/dp/B0GPDV5B12/ 9 Jun 2026] | TBA | 3 | includes the 2025 Christmas special |} ==Music== ===Theme music=== The theme music is an instrumental version of a [[Jamaica]]n song from the 1960s, "You're Wondering Now", written by [[Coxsone Dodd]], originally recorded by Andy & Joey in Jamaica. It was later made famous by [[The Skatalites]] and in [[Europe]] by [[ska]] band [[The Specials]] and later still by [[Amy Winehouse]], as featured on some editions of the deluxe version of her album ''[[Back to Black]].'' In the final scene of the first episode of the third series, the cover version recorded by The Skatalites in 1994 is played at the bar. It appeared on the official ''Death in Paradise'' soundtrack, released in January 2015, alongside other music from all four series. The original version of the song, as recorded by Andy & Joey, was played towards the end of the last episode of the sixth series. It was also recorded by [[Robert Wyatt]] on his album ''[[Mid-Eighties]]'' (1993), under the title "Alfie and Robert Sail Off Into the Sunset", only repeating the lines "You're wondering now / What to do, now you know this is the end". In the French version, the opening song is "Sunday Shining" by [[Finley Quaye]]. The theme music was given a slight overhaul in 2018, when new composer David Michael Celia joined the team and along with Magnus Fiennes, they added more bass to their theme. This theme would only last until 2020. The theme music was given another, bigger overhaul in 2021, with completely new music but still based on the original theme. It was given a new melody and bassline. The composer, Magnus Fiennes, said in an interview that the theme tune needed to be changed for its tenth anniversary. The 2021 Christmas special saw the extended version of this theme tune playing over the car with the Carib Rockets, being transported to the Carlton Villa. The lyrics were also sung over the end credits for both specials. ===Soundtrack=== In January 2015, the BBC released an official soundtrack compiling 26 songs from the first four series of the show. It contains original music for ''Death in Paradise'' and already extant tunes, though it does not include the theme music from the show. The score of the show itself is composed by [[Magnus Fiennes]] and features musicians such as the Los Angeles based Reggae band The Lions (Blake Colie on drums, Dave Wilder on bass, Dan Ubick on guitar) and keyboard/[[melodica]] player Roger Rivas. Each detective had their own personalized score based around their personality. Richard Poole had a mournful [[Clarinet|jazz clarinet]], Humphrey Goodman a [[bassoon]], Jack Mooney has a [[mandolin]], and DI Neville Parker has [[gypsy jazz]].{{Cite web |title=The story behind the music of Death in Paradise – and the new version of the theme song |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-theme-tune-new-music-soundtrack-exclusive/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |website=Radio Times |language=en}} ==Novels== The creator of the show, [[Robert Thorogood]], signed a three-book deal to write ''Death in Paradise'' novels featuring the original characters (D.I. Richard Poole, D.S. Camille Bordey, Officer Dwayne Myers, Sergeant Fidel Best and Comm. Selwyn Patterson). The first of these, ''A Meditation on Murder (A Death in Paradise novel),''{{cite book|title=A Meditation on Murder (An original Death in Paradise story): Amazon.co.uk: Robert Thorogood: 8601410743390: Books |id={{ASIN|1848453566|country=uk}} }} was published in January 2015. Early reviews were generally favourable, with the ''[[Daily Express]]'' in particular being complimentary, giving it four stars.{{cite web|last=Coates |first=Jon |url=http://www.express.co.uk/entertainment/books/555163/Book-reviews-January-s-crime-and-detective-fiction-investigated |title=Book reviews: January's crime and detective fiction investigated|work=[[Daily Express]] |publisher=[[Northern & Shell]] |date=30 January 2015 |access-date=30 March 2015}} The second book, ''The Killing of Polly Carter,'' was released in 2016. The third book, ''Death Knocks Twice,'' was released in 2017. A fourth book, ''Murder in the Caribbean,'' was published in December 2018. ==Spin-off series== In June 2022, a spin-off was announced, titled ''[[Beyond Paradise (TV series)|Beyond Paradise]]'', airing in the UK on 24 February 2023, which saw the return of Kris Marshall as Humphrey Goodman, and [[Sally Bretton]] as his fiancee Martha Lloyd as they enjoy life in Britain. The spin-off was commissioned by [[BBC One]] and [[BritBox|BritBox International]].{{cite web |title=Whatever happened to DI Humphrey Goodman? Kris Marshall and Sally Bretton reunite to star in Beyond Paradise |url=https://www.bbc.com/mediacentre/2022/beyond-paradise-death-in-paradise |website=BBC media centre |access-date=29 June 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2022/06/bbc-britbox-death-in-paradise-beyond-paradise-1235054015/|title='Death In Paradise' Spin-Off 'Beyond Paradise' Greenlit By BBC & BritBox; Kris Marshall To Star|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|first=Max|last=Goldbart|date=29 June 2022|access-date=2 July 2022}} Filming of the series started in August 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/2022/beyond-paradise-cast |title=Zahra Ahmadi, Dylan Llewellyn and Felicity Montagu join Kris Marshall and Sally Bretton as Beyond Paradise starts filming - Media Centre |website=BBC |date= |accessdate=4 August 2022}} In theory set in South Devon, it was actually filmed in Cornwall. After the first series ended, the BBC announced it had been renewed for a second series plus a Christmas special airing later in 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/2023/beyond-paradise-series-2-christmas-special|title=Hit BBC Drama Beyond Paradise to return for second series and Christmas Special |website=BBC |date= 7 April 2023|access-date= 21 April 2023}} A third series aired from 28 March to 2 May 2025, with a Christmas special in December. A fourth series aired from 27 March to 1 May, 2026. A second spin-off called ''[[Return to Paradise (2024 TV series)|Return to Paradise]]'' for ABC television in Australia and BBC One was announced in November 2023. The 6-episode series is set in the beachside hamlet of Dolphin Cove. The series was released in October 2024 on ABC-TV and iView in Australia, and in November 2024 on BBC One and iPlayer in the UK.{{cite web|url=https://help.abc.net.au/hc/en-us/articles/8330649691919-ABC-Gets-Set-for-Captivating-New-Drama-Return-to-Paradise|title=ABC Gets Set for Captivating New Drama: Return to Paradise|publisher=abc.net.au|date=15 January 2024|access-date=22 January 2024|archive-date=6 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231206162719/https://help.abc.net.au/hc/en-us/articles/8330649691919-ABC-Gets-Set-for-Captivating-New-Drama-Return-to-Paradise|url-status=dead}} A second series started airing on 31 October 2025 on BBC One. ==Adaptation== In October 2026, [[BBC Studios]] announced the first international adaptation of ''Death in Paradise'', a Croatian-language series titled {{ill|Ubojstvo u raju (Croatian TV series)|lt=''Ubojstvo u raju''|hr|Ubojstvo u raju (televizijska serija)}}. The adaptation will consist of six 60-minute episodes and is being produced by CGM Films for [[Croatian Radiotelevision]] (HRT), with plans to air on [[HRT 1]].{{cite web |title=CGM Films to produce first-ever international adaptation of BBC hit 'Death in Paradise' for HRT |url=https://redplanetpictures.co.uk/news/cgm-films-to-produce-first-ever-international-adaptation-of-bbc-hit-death-in-paradise-for-hrt |website=Red Planet Pictures |date=13 October 2026 |access-date=3 November 2026}} The series will be set in a fictional island community on the Croatian island of [[Brač]], with filming scheduled to take place in and around [[Supetar]]. Principal photography is planned to begin in spring 2027. The adaptation will be produced by Bruno Mustić and Ivan Lovreček, directed by Jelena Gavrilović, and written by Sonja Tarokić and Valentina Batalić, with Maja Fišter serving as commissioning editor for HRT.
